title: Closed Hilbert graph families and arbitrary base change
statement: Let $z:Z\to S$ and $x:X\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $z$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and $x$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For each $S$-scheme $T$ put $Z_T=Z\times_ST$, $X_T=X\times_ST$, and $W_T=Z_T\times_TX_T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $Z_T\to T$ is proper, flat and finitely presented and $X_T\to T$ is separated. For every $T$-morphism $f:Z_T\to X_T$, its actual graph map $\Gamma_f=(\mathrm{id},f):Z_T\to W_T$ [def-sfb-relative-morphisms-presheaf] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and its associated closed subscheme is a point of $\operatorname{Hilb}^{\mathrm{proper}}_{(Z\times_SX)/S}(T)$ [def-sfb-proper-hilbert-presheaf]. For every morphism $h:T'\to T$ of $S$-schemes, pullback takes any closed proper flat finitely presented family $D\subset W_T$ to another such family, and the canonical iterated-fibre-product identifications identify $(\Gamma_f)_{T'}$ with $\Gamma_{f_{T'}}$ as closed subschemes. These identifications respect identity and composite base changes. In particular $f\mapsto\Gamma_f$ defines a natural transformation $\gamma:\operatorname{Mor}_S(Z,X)\to\operatorname{Hilb}^{\mathrm{proper}}_{(Z\times_SX)/S}$.

source.place: Tag 0D1A, quot-lemma-Mor-into-Hilb, proof: graph construction and base-change permanence before the final injectivity paragraph; naturality of this construction.

proof.text: Apply the scheme base-change permanence results to $z:Z\to S$ along $T\to S$: properness is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b), flatness by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and finite presentation (local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness) by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3). Thus $Z_T\to T$ is proper, flat and finitely presented. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $W_T=Z_T\times_TX_T$ with $(Z\times_SX)\times_ST$, by the maps having the same projections to $Z,X,T$.

source.place: Tag 0D1A, quot-lemma-Mor-into-Hilb, proof, base-change permanence and the displayed graph target.

proof.text: The diagonal $X_T\to X_T\times_TX_T$ is the pullback of $X\to X\times_SX$: maps into either pullback specify two maps into $X$ and one into $T$, with the same two $X$-maps. This follows directly from [def-pc-fibre-product]. The original diagonal is closed by separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]; its pullback is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Hence $X_T\to T$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 03KL, lemma-base-change-separated, proof, restricted to schemes.

proof.text: Write $P=Z_T\times_TX_T$. The graph [def-sfb-relative-morphisms-presheaf] is the pullback of the diagonal of $X_T/T$ along $(f\circ\operatorname{pr}_Z,\operatorname{pr}_X):P\to X_T\times_TX_T$. Indeed a map into that pullback is a pair $(a:U\to Z_T,b:U\to X_T)$ with $f\circ a=b$; it is uniquely determined by $a$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes the actual graph a closed immersion. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] it identifies $Z_T$ with its closed subscheme $D_f$ in $P$. Under this identification the structure map of $D_f$ is $Z_T\to T$, since $\operatorname{pr}_Z\circ\Gamma_f=\mathrm{id}$. Step 1 and [def-sfb-proper-hilbert-presheaf] give the required Hilbert point.

source.place: Tag 0D1A, quot-lemma-Mor-into-Hilb, proof, graph construction and membership in Hilb; graph pullback expanded from spaces-morphisms-lemma-semi-diagonal.

proof.text: For $h:T\prime\to T$ and a closed subscheme $D\subset W_T$, let $r:W_{T\prime}\to W_T$ be the base-change map. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $D\times_{W_T}W_{T\prime}\cong D\times_TT\prime$, compatibly with inclusion into $W_{T\prime}$. By [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image], this inclusion is closed and its defining ideal is $\operatorname{im}(r^*\mathcal I_D\to\mathcal O_{W_{T\prime}})$, precisely ideal pullback in [def-sfb-proper-hilbert-presheaf]. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b), [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3), applied to $D\to T$ along $h$, its structure map to $T\prime$ is proper, flat and finitely presented. This proves permanence for every such family without a flatness assumption on $h$.

source.place: Tag 01JU, lemma-fibre-product-immersion (1), and quot.tex Tag 0CZY, situation-hilb, base-change paragraph.

proof.text: For $D=D_f$, the identification $Z_T\times_TT\prime\cong Z_{T\prime}$ sends its pulled-back inclusion into $W_{T\prime}=Z_{T\prime}\times_{T\prime}X_{T\prime}$ to $(\mathrm{id},f_{T\prime})$: its first projection is the identity and its second is the base-changed morphism. These two projection equalities uniquely determine the inclusion by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus the pullback and $\Gamma_{f_{T\prime}}$ are isomorphic over the ambient scheme, and their structure-sheaf maps have the same kernel [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. They consequently define the same closed subscheme, not merely the same underlying closed subset.

source.place: Tag 0D1A, quot-lemma-Mor-into-Hilb, naturality of the graph construction, expanded using the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: For the identity of $T$, the comparison maps have the original projections, so uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] makes them identity comparisons. For $T\prime\prime\xrightarrow{k}T\prime\xrightarrow{h}T$, both the iterated comparison and the comparison for $h\circ k$ have the same projections to $Z,X,T\prime\prime$; uniqueness makes them equal. The induced identifications of closed subschemes also agree because they commute with the inclusions. Therefore Step 5 says exactly $\operatorname{Hilb}^{\mathrm{proper}}(h)(D_f)=D_{\operatorname{Mor}(h)(f)}$ for the two presheaf maps [def-sfb-relative-morphisms-presheaf, def-sfb-proper-hilbert-presheaf]. The maps $f\mapsto D_f$ form the asserted natural transformation.

source.place: Tag 0D1A, quot-lemma-Mor-into-Hilb, natural transformation, identity and composition checked by uniqueness.

lean.statement: theorem hilbert_graph_family_base_change {Z X S : Scheme.{u}} (z : Z ⟶ S) (x : X ⟶ S) [IsProper z] [Flat z] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation z] [IsSeparated x] : (∀ T : Over S, IsProper (pullback.fst T.hom z) ∧ Flat (pullback.fst T.hom z) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (pullback.fst T.hom z) ∧ IsSeparated (pullback.fst T.hom x)) ∧ (∀ (T T' : Over S) (h : T' ⟶ T) (D : (properHilbertPresheaf (pullback.fst z x ≫ z)).obj (op T)), IsProperHilbertFamily (pullback.fst z x ≫ z) T' (D.1.comap (baseChangeMap (pullback.fst z x ≫ z) h))) ∧ ∃ γ : relativeMorphismsPresheaf z x ⟶ properHilbertPresheaf (pullback.fst z x ≫ z), (∀ (T : Over S) (f : (relativeMorphismsPresheaf z x).obj (op T)), IsClosedImmersion (relativeMorphismGraph z x T f) ∧ (γ.app (op T) f).1 = (relativeMorphismGraph z x T f).ker) ∧ (∀ (T T' : Over S) (h : T' ⟶ T) (f : (relativeMorphismsPresheaf z x).obj (op T)), (relativeMorphismGraph z x T f).ker.comap (baseChangeMap (pullback.fst z x ≫ z) h) = (relativeMorphismGraph z x T' ((relativeMorphismsPresheaf z x).map h.op f)).ker) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (D : (properHilbertPresheaf (pullback.fst z x ≫ z)).obj (op T)), D.1.comap (baseChangeMap (pullback.fst z x ≫ z) (𝟙 T)) = D.1) ∧ (∀ (T T' T'' : Over S) (h : T' ⟶ T) (k : T'' ⟶ T') (D : (properHilbertPresheaf (pullback.fst z x ≫ z)).obj (op T)), (D.1.comap (baseChangeMap (pullback.fst z x ≫ z) h)).comap (baseChangeMap (pullback.fst z x ≫ z) k) = D.1.comap (baseChangeMap (pullback.fst z x ≫ z) (k ≫ h)))
